newsitem.title: USA: HelpMate furloughs staff, faces eviction.
newsitem.headline: HelpMate furloughs staff, faces eviction.

text.p: HelpMate Robotics Inc (HRI) said a cash shortage at the company will result in the furlough of all "but a minimal crew" of its employees, effective August 4.
In a news release, HRI also disclosed that its landlord has served an eviction notice to the company for non-payment of rent.
HRI said it has not been unsuccessful in negotiations with Leasing Technologies Inc (LTI) for the sale and lease-back of additional HelpMate robots.
HRI is in default under its Master Lease Agreement with LTI. It said it is using its "best efforts to correct these deficiencies in a timely fashion."
In the next two weeks, HRI Chief Executive Thomas Sweeny and Chairman Joseph Engelberger will seek alternative sources of working capital, the company said.

During this period, HRI staff will be able to provide, maintenance and support for hospital clients where HelpMate Robots are in operation. While the furlough is in effect, HRI will discontinue its sales and marketing efforts and the company will limit its production to fill only a portion of its backlog of existing orders.
If it cannot raise financing, HRI said it will consider seeking a buyer or "seeking refuge under laws designed to protect the rights of debtors."
